title: Define the federation policy
breadcrumb: Federation Hub: connecting multiple TAK Servers

blocks.html:
The policy is the heart of the hub: a graph that says which connected servers exist and how data may flow between them. Until a policy is active, nothing federates — and the hub denies any server not in the active policy.

Open the Policy Manager

In a browser go to **https://<hub>:9100/index.html** and authenticate with the cert (or Keycloak admin) you authorized in Establish trust. Choose New to start a blank policy, or Load an existing one. You're then in the Policy Editor — a drag-and-drop graph canvas.

The node types

Drag these from the palette onto the canvas:

CA Group

Represents the CA of a TAK Server (or another hub) that wants to connect. Pick the CA you uploaded earlier (by issuer/subject). Two options:

  • Interconnected — if several servers share the same CA, they auto-link and share all data. Usually off (run unique certs per server).
  • Allow Token Auth — auto-accept incoming connections that present a client cert over TLS and receive a token (instead of full mTLS). Token Auth Duration -1 = never expires.

Each Deploy App TAK Server you federate gets one CA Group node.

Outgoing

A connection initiated from this hub to another TAK Server or hub (this is what enables multi-hop). Enter the remote Host and Port, optionally use token auth, and tick Outgoing Enabled when ready.

Token Group

A set of tokens that servers can use to connect to this hub. Generate and manage tokens here (-1 = no expiry). Unlike a CA Group's Allow Token Auth (a server is auto-issued a token by presenting its cert), a Token Group is manual — you send each server's admin a token, and a fresh one when it expires.

Connect nodes with edges

Draw edges between nodes to begin federating data. Edges are unidirectional — drag from the source node and drop on the destination; the arrow shows the direction data flows. To make a two-way link, draw an edge each way. When you create an edge, a form asks how to filter what crosses it — see Control what crosses.

So "Server A may send to Server B" is: a CA Group for A, a CA Group for B, and an edge A → B with the filtering you choose.

Activate the policy

Edits to the graph aren't live until you save and upload the policy — click the cloud icon in the top toolbar. Once active:

  • Federates in the policy may connect (the hub denies anyone not in it).
  • A green node indicates a successful connection.

Re-upload after every change (add/edit/delete a node, add a connection, generate tokens) for it to take effect.
